contexts.text: To be reconciled to thy brother () = charity towards the neighbour. ( = to shun enmity, hatred, and revenge. DLife 73.) ( = worship from charity. AE 391:20.)
The Lord teaches the good of love... by reconciliation with the neighbour.
(These two statements are thus reconciled.) CL 76:4.
(These conjugial simulations) are for the sake of reconciliations. Explained.
(For a wife) can be reconciled in a moment.
With the evil, although the internal is reconciled, these (evil feelings) lie concealed...
(The notion that God) wants to be reconciled...
They are never reconciled except by being adored as gods.
Those who have hated each other, meet there, and attempt many evils against each other... Hence the Lord says that those who are enemies ought to be reconciled. Illustrated.
The brother having ought against thee = anger, enmity, or hatred; and to be reconciled = the dissipation of these, and the consequent conjunction by love.
Nor can God be reconciled except by the repentance of man himself.
2. To an enemy, man performs the uses of repentance or reconciliation.
